newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable, await INRO.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable, await INRO.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were stable in late trading on Friday with traders watching for possible intervention by the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) to prop up prices.
"Our fate will depend on INRO's decision...because we expect to see something happen. In general, traders think that prices will slip further," said one trader in Padang, West Sumatra.
INRO's five-day indicator dipped on July 10 to 182.48 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg, a level where the group may buy rubber from the market.

But an INRO official in Kuala Lumpur hinted on Friday that the group would not intervene in the market unless the indicator price fell to 172 cents, the level where INRO was obliged to buy rubber from the market.
Indonesian traders said INRO was obliged to buy rubber from the market when the level was below 40.00 U.S. cents/lb for the benchmark tyre-grade SIR20.
On the other hand, the international rubber group may buy rubber when prices hover at 42.00, said the traders.
"This means that prices must fall further before INRO really intervenes in the market. The sentiment remains bearish as we don't see much buying interest," said one trader.
"I think INRO will become the sole buyer because buying interest from elsewhere is almost zero," he said.
Traders said whether or not INRO's expected intervention will be successful would depend on how much rubber it would buy and also for how long.
"I don't think it will help if INRO only buys 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes. They should purchase at least between 50,000 and 100,000 tonnes," said one trader.
Traders said offer prices were quoted at 43.50 fob Medan for September shipment, 43.00 fob Padang and Surabaya, 43.25 fob Palembang and 42.75 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
